title: "4.6 Sensitivity and stress"
order: 6
---

## Method

Each scenario refits the scorecard with `train.py`'s own recipe — the same split, the same
`BinningProcess`, logistic regression and scaling — on a reduced set of columns, and
measures the refit on the same held-out applicants (`wiki/facts/score_stress.py`). The
bureau scenario drops columns from the committed {{< var score.n_features >}} and keeps
`train.py`'s default binning solver; the three raw-column scenarios bin raw data columns
and use the mixed-integer solver ([4.3](methodology.qmd#implementation-note-the-binning-solver)).

The refits take minutes, so they are cached in the facts and re-run by
`python verify.py --full` (or `make wiki-facts-full`), not on every run.

{{< include ../../_generated/score-stress.md >}}

## Bureau feed down: a gate failure, documented

If the credit bureau feed fails, the model loses {{< var score.stress.bureau_columns >}}.
Refitted without them, the scorecard reaches a held-out AUC of
{{< var score.stress.no_bureau.auc >}} (KS {{< var score.stress.no_bureau.ks >}}), **below
the {{< var score.gate >}} gate**.

That result is kept as it is. The gate is not lowered for the scenario and the refit is
not tuned until it passes: the failure is the result. It says the model's performance
depends on the bureau feed, so a scorecard refitted without it is not the validated model
and may not replace it. The consequence for operations: an applicant whose bureau data are
missing cannot be scored by this model as validated. The documented response is to refer
such an applicant to an underwriter rather than score it on partial inputs. The platform
does not implement that rule today, because its generated data have no missing values; a
production implementation would have to. As the code stands, a missing bureau value would
not stop scoring at all: `compute_features` would score it as zero
([4.2](data.qmd#features)).

{{< yt S2-c4 >}}

## Five raw columns: most of the signal is in a few features

Five raw columns — {{< var score.stress.five_raw_columns >}}, all of them in the
generator's default logit — reach a held-out AUC of {{< var score.stress.five_raw.auc >}}
on their own: at the gate, by a margin far smaller than the
±{{< var score.auc_ci_half >}} interval half-width ([4.5](performance.qmd#discrimination)).
Most of what the full card ranks on is carried by a handful of causal features. This
agrees with the variance shares in [4.3](methodology.qmd#feature-selection-and-signal).

## Structural zeros: nothing to rank on

Five of the columns the generator gives no role in default —
{{< var score.stress.structural_five_columns >}} — refit to a held-out AUC of
{{< var score.stress.structural_five.auc >}}: a coin toss. Three of them are in the
committed model; this scenario is the direct evidence that they cannot rank applicants,
and the reason finding 3 in [4.7](limitations.qmd) treats them as inert.

## Revenue and its relatives: real but limited signal

The last scenario keeps {{< var score.stress.proxy_five_columns >}}. Of these, only
`annual_revenue` is in the generator's default logit. Three of the others are each
`annual_revenue` times a multiplier (`shared/data_generator.py`):

- `requested_amount`: revenue times a random draw — noise, so its signal is borrowed from
  revenue alone;
- `net_income`: revenue times `profit_margin`, and `total_debt`: revenue times `leverage`.
  Both multipliers are causal primitives in the generator, but the product does not isolate
  them: each column mixes the multiplier's effect with revenue's scale.

`employees` has no role at all; it is another of the generator's structural zeros. Together
the five reach {{< var score.stress.proxy_five.auc >}}: real, stable ranking, carried by
revenue and by what its products happen to carry of two causal ratios. A proxy ranks for someone else's
reasons ([glossary](../../reference/glossary.qmd)), and a model built on proxies would
fail as soon as the relationship to the causal feature changed.

## What the scenarios establish

- The committed card passes; one realistic operational failure — the bureau feed — does
  not, and the chapter says so rather than moving the gate.
- The model's discrimination rests on the causal features, not on the structural zeros it
  also contains.
- Each column set is fixed in `wiki/facts/score_stress.py`, so every scenario reruns
  identically and a changed result is a changed model or data, not a changed test.
